items.title: New way to issue school zone parking tickets launched in Mississauga
items.summary: Those who park illegally in Mississauga school zones can no longer avoid fines by simply speeding away before a parking enforcement officer reaches their vehicle. Starting Oct. 1, City of Mississauga parking enforcement is using Licence Plate Recognition technology to dish out parking tickets. LPR cameras will scan the plates of illegally parked cars and the city will mail the infraction notices to offenders/registered vehicle owners. “This new process supports parking enforcement officers in places where issuing a physical penalty notice on a vehicle may not be effective, such as school zones and time-limited parking zones,” city officials said, adding officers will continue to place tickets on vehicle windshields when the situation allows. ” The city added it’s initially using the technology in school zones “to help improve road safety and traffic flow around schools, with expansion to additional locations” in 2027. Using Licence Plate Recognition technology comes just over a year after the city increased parking fines across Mississauga, in some cases significant hikes. As of April 2025, illegally stopping in a school zone costs offenders $145 (up from $65 prior to the hikes). By using Licence Plate Recognition technology, the city says it will also improve safety for parking enforcement officers and enhance how the municipality delivers services. The new technology is among a series of changes introduced this month by the city’s parking enforcement division.

items.title: Mississauga's SAWITRI Theatre and Very Serious Theatre Company present "the joshis"
items.summary: SAWITRI Theatre Group and Very Serious Theatre Company (VSTC) are proud to present the joshis, a contemporary Canadian play written by Max Kingsbury and directed by Devansh Shah and Raina Desai. The production runs from October 22nd–30th, 2026, at AN1 Studios in Mississauga. Written in English, the joshis (pronounced joe-shes) it is a play about a family gathered to celebrate the festive season of lights, but as the celebration reaches its peak, a dramatic turn of events changes their lives forever! Content Warnings: Strong Language, suitable for ages 14+ "SAWITRI Theatre Group is redefining how culturally rooted stories can move, challenge, and unite contemporary audiences,” says Jasmine Sawant the Founder & Artistic Co-Director. Founded in 2003, SAWITRI Theatre Group is an award-winning not-for-profit theatre company based in Mississauga, Ontario. Under the leadership of Jasmine Sawant and Shruti Shah, SAWITRI has produced more than 93 works, including 23 full-length plays across four languages: English, Marathi, Gujarati, and Hindi. Recognized for its innovative and risk-taking approach, SAWITRI is committed to staging culturally specific stories with universal resonance. The company creates space for intergenerational and intercultural dialogue while providing meaningful opportunities for both emerging and established artists. With a mandate to inform, entertain, and heal, SAWITRI continues to shape Canada’s theatrical landscape through bold storytelling and deep community engagement. SAWITRI Theatre is also the producer and presenter of the Mississauga Multilingual Fringe Festival (MMFF), the only multilingual fringe festival in North America. Operationally, SAWITRI Theatre Group is partly funded by the City of Mississauga and the Ontario Arts Council, as well as by The Open Space, Nitin Sawant, and the unstinting support of family, friends and volunteers.

items.title: Mississauga Fire Fighters Association endorses Bonnie Crombie for mayor
items.summary: Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie has secured the endorsement of the city’s firefighters’ association. The group said Crombie’s community safety plan will strengthen emergency services, improve 911 response times and invest in mental-health support. “Firefighters know that keeping a community safe takes leadership, preparation and a willingness to listen to the people on the front lines,” Chris Varcoe, President of the Mississauga Fire Fighters Association, wrote in a statement. “We are endorsing Bonnie Crombie because we trust her to work with us, support our members and make the safety of Mississauga families a priority,” he added. Crombie previously held the City’s top job from 2014 to 2024, but left that position to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. After bringing the Liberals to a third-place finish in the 2025 Ontario general election and failing to secure a seat in the legislature, the party triggered a leadership review. Crombie received 57 per cent support, but the lacklustre results led to her resignation as OLP leader at the beginning of this year. She’s now looking to return to her old job as mayor of Mississauga and will face off against incumbent mayor Carolyn Parrish.

items.title: Peel Police Identify Suspect Vehicle as 1999-2005 Chevrolet Silverado in Fatal Dundas Street Hit-and-Run
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, investigators have identified the type of vehicle involved in Tuesday evening's fatal hit-and-run on Dundas Street West in Mississauga. Police say a pedestrian was crossing in a crosswalk when a dark-coloured pickup truck travelling south on Winston Churchill Boulevard turned west onto Dundas Street West and struck him, then fled the scene without stopping. Officers, firefighters and paramedics arrived and attempted life-saving measures, but the man was pronounced dead at the scene. He has been described only as a man in his 60s, and police have not released his name. On Wednesday, Const. Tyler Bell-Morena told reporters that investigators have now narrowed down the suspect vehicle to a 1999 to 2005 model year Chevrolet Silverado 500 series pickup truck, two-tone in colour. Police released surveillance video showing the moments leading up to the collision in hopes the footage will help the public identify the driver. Investigators say they believe it is only a matter of time before the person responsible is found and are urging anyone with information to come forward.

items.title: 500,000 Jobs Already Surround Pearson Airport as Ottawa Weighs a Private Operator
items.summary: According to a column published by Insauga, the federal government's plan to install a private operator at Toronto Pearson International Airport could mean far more for Mississauga than higher fees or extra noise. The piece, written by a former Greater Toronto Airports Authority employee, argues that Pearson's real asset is its location, since the airport sits on 1,867 hectares of federal land at the centre of Canada's second-largest employment zone. Citing a 2025 Deloitte study prepared for the GTAA, the column notes that zone already supports more than 500,000 jobs, many of them in Mississauga, with access to highways 401, 427, 409 and 407 as well as the Kitchener GO line and the UP Express. The author suggests a new ownership model could eventually turn parts of the airport lands into an urban hub resembling the airport cities built in parts of Asia and Europe. Pearson is currently run by the GTAA, which leases the federal land and operates its buildings and runways to fund upkeep and growth. The column frames Prime Minister Mark Carney's privatization plan as a shift in who controls that existing model rather than an entirely new concept, and argues the underlying economics make the idea worth watching closely.

New athletic centre officially opens at TFS – Canada’s International School in Mississauga
items.summary: Upcoming open houses will let parents and families get a look at the spacious new centre that recently opened at TFS – Canada’s International School in Mississauga. Known as Canada’s first French immersion school, the Toronto French School’s West Campus in Lakeview celebrated the start of the new school year with a ribbon-cutting for the new centre, which brings 12,600 sq. ft of additional space to the school. The expansion, funded in part by generous contributions from many of the school’s parents, alumni and staff, includes Gymnase Kaneff (a junior regulation-sized gymnasium well-equipped for hosting home games and tournaments); Galerie Bechara (a beautiful viewing gallery overlooking the gymnasium); as well as an inviting new school entrance and upgraded classrooms. The new centre also features an impressive state-of-the-art design studio outfitted with cutting-edge technology for students to learn practical engineering, robotics, and creative problem solving. A series of open houses and guided tours will offer an opportunity to explore the new centre firsthand over the coming months. The new centre is designed to help students pursue their passions, gain confidence and strengthen their leadership and teamwork abilities, while also serving families and the broader Mississauga community for generations to come. The spacious centre with its premium facilities contributes to Toronto French School’s reputation as a place for students to learn and thrive in an inclusive community. The school is renowned as the only bilingual and full continuum IB World School in Canada, providing a high-quality and internationally focused education that’s designed to develop students’ knowledge and skills both inside and outside the classroom. To celebrate the new athletic centre, Toronto Raptors star Scottie Barnes attended the grand opening for a Q&A session with students, and led them through a series of fun basketball drills..

items.title: Height Lowered to 37 Storeys as Ontario Tribunal Settles Erin Mills Mall Redevelopment Fight
items.summary: According to Insauga, a nine-tower redevelopment of the Erin Mills Town Centre property has won approval through a settlement at the Ontario Land Tribunal. The plan covers the mall's northwest quadrant at 5100 Erin Mills Parkway, where existing restaurants and shops would be demolished to make way for the project. The original proposal called for towers ranging from 20 to 44 storeys and totalling 3,162 units, a scale that drew opposition from residents at public meetings held in 2025. Neighbours raised concerns about building heights, a lack of affordable and rental units, and the loss of existing retail space in the area. The property owner appealed to the tribunal after arguing that city council had failed to act on the official plan amendment and rezoning applications, and the tribunal holds the authority to override municipal decisions in such cases. Mississauga and the developer ultimately reached a settlement, approved by the tribunal last week, that trims the maximum height to 37 storeys while keeping nine towers in the plan. The revised proposal also adds a public park, an urban plaza and a new pedestrian and road network, with construction expected to proceed in phases.
